record.paper_title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics
record.original_question: For the multidimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations, are basic nonlinear wave patterns such as planar viscous shock profiles, viscous rarefaction waves, and contact waves nonlinearly stable under generic multidimensional perturbations? Can one also determine the leading-order, or even higher-order, large-time asymptotic ansatz for solutions whose initial data are small perturbations of these wave patterns?

evidence.quote: Large time asymptotic states for the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations. ... It is of great interest to know whether basic nonlinear wave patterns such as planar viscous shock profiles and viscous rarefaction waves, and contact waves are nonlinearly stable under generic multi-dimensional perturbations. Can one determine the leading order (or even higher order) asymptotic ansatz of a solution to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations when its initial data are small perturbations of these basic wave patterns?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the compressible Navier–Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\ge 2$,
$$\partial_t \rho + \operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0,\qquad \partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u)+\nabla p(\rho)=\mu\Delta u+(\mu+\lambda)\nabla\operatorname{div} u,$$
(possibly augmented by an energy equation when temperature is included), where $\rho>0$ is the density, $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$ the velocity, $p$ a smooth pressure law with $p'(\rho)>0$, and $\mu>0$, $2\mu+\lambda>0$ the viscosity coefficients. A planar viscous shock profile is a traveling-wave solution of the form $(\rho,u)(t,x)=(\bar\rho,\bar u)(x_1-st)$ connecting two distinct Rankine–Hugoniot–compatible end states $(\rho_\pm,u_\pm)$. A planar viscous rarefaction wave is the self-similar smooth solution of the corresponding one-dimensional problem associated to a genuinely nonlinear rarefaction Riemann data, lifted to $\mathbb{R}^d$ as a function of $x_1/t$. A planar viscous contact wave is the diffusive profile associated to a linearly degenerate Riemann discontinuity in the one-dimensional system.

(a) Prove or disprove that each of these basic planar wave patterns (viscous shock profile, viscous rarefaction wave, viscous contact wave) is nonlinearly asymptotically stable in $\mathbb{R}^d$ under generic small multidimensional perturbations of the initial data—i.e., perturbations depending on all variables $(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, not merely on $x_1$, and not subject to zero-mass or other artificial restrictions.

(b) For initial data that are small multidimensional perturbations of such a wave pattern, determine the leading-order (and, if possible, higher-order) large-time asymptotic ansatz describing the solution as $t\to\infty$, including the precise shifts, modulations, and dispersive/diffusive corrections needed to capture the asymptotics.
artifact.status_search_result: Significant recent progress exists. Nonlinear stability of planar viscous shock waves for the 3D compressible Navier–Stokes equations under generic multidimensional perturbations (without zero-mass condition) has been established via a-contraction with time-dependent shift methods (Kang–Vasseur–Wang, JEMS, arXiv:2204.09428), and related results cover Navier–Stokes–Poisson and relaxed systems, as well as planar shocks with spatial oscillations. Multidimensional stability of large-amplitude profiles, the full picture for rarefaction and contact waves under generic multi-D perturbations, and precise higher-order asymptotic ansätze remain incompletely resolved, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear stability of planar viscous shock wave to three-dimensional compressible Navier–Stokes equations (JEMS)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes nonlinear stability up to time-dependent shift of planar viscous shock for 3D compressible Navier–Stokes under generic perturbations.
status_evidence.claim: Planar viscous shock stability under generic 3D perturbations has been proved.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2204.09428
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlinear stability of planar viscous shock wave to 3D compressible Navier-Stokes equations, no zero-mass condition.
status_evidence.claim: Key partial-resolution result for the shock case.

status_evidence.title: Time-asymptotic stability of planar Navier-Stokes shocks with spatial oscillations
status_evidence.snippet: Extends multidimensional time-asymptotic stability of planar Navier-Stokes shocks.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:2511.07799
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic stability of planar viscous shock waves for 3D relaxed compressible Navier-Stokes equations.
status_evidence.claim: Active ongoing work on related systems.

status_evidence.title: Multidimensional Stability of Large-Amplitude Navier–Stokes Shocks
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient stability conditions in multi-D differ from 1D by codimension-one set.
status_evidence.claim: Large-amplitude multi-D case remains subtle and not fully resolved.
